copy.headline: Denmark, Greenland and US sign security deal opening two new bases in Greenland

extended.text: The three government leaders of Denmark, Greenland and the United States signed a new security agreement for Greenland in New York on Tuesday afternoon, at the UN General Assembly. The United States may build two new bases, at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, and the agreement has no end date.

It reaffirms Denmark's sovereignty over Greenland. The United States commits to prioritise Greenlandic companies when it builds the bases and has reconfirmed a 35-year-old promise to remove its waste from the country.

Jens-Frederik Nielsen, Greenland's head of government, landed in Nuuk on Wednesday evening and says the agreement secures Greenland's self-determination. 'To look your own people in the eye and have delivered what we want, that we shape our own future ourselves, that is moving,' Múte B. Egede told a kaffemik in Nuuk.

Altinget's analysis reads the deal as keeping sovereignty and self-determination with Denmark and Greenland while markedly strengthening America's military hold, at a high price. The New York Times judges it well short of Trump's demand to make the island a US territory.

copy.headline: Trump greets Xi on the tarmac as US and China extend trade truce to 10 January

standard.text: The United States and China will extend last year's pause in their trade conflict until 10 January, treasury secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday as Xi Jinping landed for a state visit. The talks cover trade, AI and Taiwan.
Donald and Melania Trump met Xi and his wife at Joint Base Andrews with a 30-metre red carpet, a military band and two B-1 bombers overhead, an airport welcome the Washington Post calls unusual.
DR's analysis says an AI deal needs trust that does not exist between the two, and observers cited by Politiken point out Xi can argue that if Trump may control Greenland, China may control Taiwan.

short.text: The US and China will extend their trade-war pause until 10 January, treasury secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday, as Donald Trump greeted Xi Jinping on the tarmac with a red carpet and a B-1 flyover before the summit.

copy.headline: Nationalbanken doubles growth forecast to 4 per cent, warns against spending

standard.text: Nationalbanken on Wednesday raised its forecast for Danish growth to 4 per cent this year, double its previous expectation, with pharmaceutical production abroad the main driver despite tariffs and war.
House prices are now expected to rise 8.6 per cent this year, 4.6 per cent in 2027 and 2.9 per cent in 2028.

Christian Kettel Thomsen, Nationalbanken's governor, tells Berlingske the government 'must refrain from feeding into that situation with fiscal policy', warning that defence rearmament, the food cheque and the electricity tax cut lift consumption and risk higher inflation. The finance bill is expected around Folketinget's opening on Tuesday 6 October.

short.text: Nationalbanken on Wednesday doubled its forecast for Danish growth to 4 per cent this year, driven by pharmaceutical production abroad, while its governor, Christian Kettel Thomsen, tells Berlingske the government must hold back spending in the finance bill to avoid high inflation.

copy.deck: Pharmaceutical output abroad drives the upgrade; house prices are set to rise 8.6 per cent this year.

copy.headline: Government halts new pig production for twelve months

standard.text: The government on Wednesday imposed a temporary halt on new conventional pig production, lasting 12 months. Until new rules for pig production are drawn up, it is forbidden to establish or expand conventional pig farms.
Venstre will not back the halt, although the party agrees that the country's pigs need better welfare, its animal-welfare spokesperson Marie Bjerre tells Berlingske.

copy.headline: Vänsterpartiet MP-elect takes 'timeout' as Swedish vote-fraud inquiry widens

standard.text: Mohamed Ali, elected for Vänsterpartiet with 648 votes in Borlänge, has agreed a 'timeout' with the party over vote-fraud accusations he rejects; according to Swedish media cited by Politiken, it offered him a job to withdraw.

Vänsterpartiet, fourth largest on 8.4 per cent, has demanded ministerial posts. Johan Varning Bendtsen, Kristeligt Dagblad's Nordic correspondent, writes that it is now far from government and Swedish analysts speculate about a Magdalena Andersson minority government, alone or with Miljöpartiet.
A fraud report two weeks before the vote was dropped; a second, filed on election day, is investigated at top police level, and a third person joined the case on Wednesday.

short.text: Mohamed Ali, elected for Vänsterpartiet in Borlänge, has agreed a 'timeout' with the party over vote-fraud accusations he rejects; Kristeligt Dagblad's Johan Varning Bendtsen writes the party is now far from government.

copy.headline: AI chiefs tell UN Security Council to keep the technology under human control

standard.text: Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic told the UN Security Council on Wednesday that international cooperation is needed to keep artificial intelligence under human control, calling on nations to work together on regulation.

Altman said the technology's development requires 'extreme care', while an AI executive quoted by Børsen warned that 'the race threatens every nation'. On Tuesday, from the same building, Trump promised to keep the US ahead of China.
